column2: Green turf sloped down to either edge, brown snaky tree-roots gleamed below the surface of the quiet water, while ahead of them the silvery shoulder and foamy tumble of a weir, arm-in-arm with a restless dripping mill-wheel, that held up in its turn a grey-gabled millhouse, filled the air with a soothing murmur of sound, dull and smothery, yet with little clear voices speaking up cheerfully out of it at intervals.
column3: turf 草皮；snaky 像蛇一样弯曲的；gleam 闪光；soothing 让人安心的
column4: while 后面这一部分，谓语是哪个词？
column6: Green turf sloped … brown snaky tree-roots gleamed … the silvery shoulder … foamy tumble … filled
column7: Green turf sloped down to either edge, / brown snaky tree-roots gleamed / below the surface of the quiet water, / while ahead of them / the silvery shoulder and foamy tumble of a weir, / arm-in-arm with a restless dripping mill-wheel, / that held up in its turn a grey-gabled millhouse, / filled the air with a soothing murmur of sound, / dull and smothery, / yet with little clear voices / speaking up cheerfully out of it at intervals.
column8: 绿草坡一直斜铺到两边水边，／褐色的树根像蛇一样，闪着光，／在平静的水面下；／而在他们前方，／拦河坝银亮的坝肩和翻滚的白沫，／挽着一架不停滴水的水车，／这（水车）又托着一座灰山墙的磨坊，／让空气里满是叫人安心的低语声，／闷闷的，含混不清，／却有几个清亮的小声音，／时不时欢快地从（这声音）里冒出来。
column9: 读到 that held up 容易以为谓语来了。held 是从句里的动词，这个从句修饰紧挨着的 mill-wheel；while 分句的谓语是后面的 filled。
column10: 绿草坡一直铺到两边水边，褐色的树根像蛇一样，在平静的水面下发亮；前方，一道拦河坝银亮的坝肩和翻滚的白沫，挽着一架不停滴水的水车，水车又托着一座灰色山墙的磨坊，让空气里满是叫人安心的低语声，闷闷的，含混不清，却不时有几个清亮的小声音欢快地从里面冒出来。
column12: The Wind in the Willows 第 1 章 句 5

column2: The old grey horse, dreaming, as he plodded along, of his quiet paddock, in a new raw situation such as this, simply abandoned himself to his natural emotions.
column7: The old grey horse, / dreaming, / as he plodded along, / of his quiet paddock, / in a new raw situation such as this, / simply abandoned himself to his natural emotions.
column8: 那匹老灰马，／正做着梦，／（一边）慢吞吞地走着，／梦见他那片安静的小草场，／碰上这样一个从没见过的局面，／干脆什么都不管，由着本性来了。
column9: abandoned himself to his natural emotions 不是“抛弃了自己”。abandon oneself to sth 是“完全听凭（某种情绪）摆布”：马不再听使唤，由着本能的情绪来了。
column10: 那匹老灰马一边慢吞吞地走，一边梦着他那片安静的小草场，碰上这样一个从没见过的局面，干脆完全由着本能的情绪来了。
column12: The Wind in the Willows 第 2 章 卡句 2

column2: Somehow, it soon seemed taken for granted by all three of them that the trip was a settled thing; and the Rat, though still unconvinced in his mind, allowed his good-nature to override his personal objections.
column3: unconvinced 没被说服的；override 压倒，盖过
column4: 真正的主语是哪一部分？
column5: that the trip was a settled thing
column7: Somehow, / it soon seemed taken for granted / by all three of them / that the trip was a settled thing; / and the Rat, / though still unconvinced in his mind, / allowed his good-nature to override his personal objections.
column8: 不知怎么，／很快，（这件事）好像成了不用说的／三个都这么看／——就是这趟旅行已经定了；／而河鼠，／虽然心里还没服气，／却由着自己的好脾气压下了个人的反对。
column9: taken for granted 不是“被准许”。take sth for granted 是“认为理所当然”，这里是被动：三个都把去旅行当成了已经定下的事。
column10: 不知怎么，三个很快都默认这趟旅行已经定了；河鼠心里虽然还是不服，也由着自己的好脾气压下了个人的反对。
column12: The Wind in the Willows 第 2 章 句 1

column2: Something up above was calling him imperiously, and he made for the steep little tunnel which answered in his case to the gravelled carriage-drive owned by animals whose residences are nearer to the sun and air.
column3: imperiously 不容分说地；tunnel 地道；gravelled 铺了砾石的；residence 住宅
column4: owned by animals 修饰哪个词？
column6: Something … was calling … he made for
column7: Something up above was calling him imperiously, / and he made for the steep little tunnel / which answered in his case / to the gravelled carriage-drive / owned by animals / whose residences are nearer to the sun and air.
column8: 上面有什么东西在不容分说地召唤他，／他朝那条又陡又小的隧道奔去，／这（隧道）对他来说相当于／铺砾石的马车道——／（那种车道）归一些动物所有，／（这些动物）的住处离阳光和空气更近。
column9: answered to 不是“回答”。answer to sth 在这里是“相当于，对应”：鼹鼠家这条又陡又小的隧道，相当于地面上的人家门前那条铺砾石的车道。
column10: 上面有什么东西在不容分说地召唤他。他朝那条又陡又小的隧道奔去。对他来说，这条隧道就相当于那些住处离阳光和空气更近的动物家门前铺着砾石的马车道。
column12: The Wind in the Willows 第 1 章 句 1

column2: He was bowled over in an instant by the impatient and contemptuous Mole, who trotted along the side of the hedge chaffing the other rabbits as they peeped hurriedly from their holes to see what the row was about.
column3: contemptuous 瞧不起人的；trot 小跑；chaff 取笑；peep 探头看
column4: as 引出的从句，谓语是哪个词？
column7: He was bowled over in an instant / by the impatient and contemptuous Mole, / who trotted along the side of the hedge / chaffing the other rabbits / as they peeped hurriedly from their holes / to see what the row was about.
column8: 他（老兔子）一眨眼就被撞翻了，／撞他的是又急又瞧不起人的鼹鼠，／他（鼹鼠）沿着树篱一路小跑，／（鼹鼠）边跑边取笑别的兔子，／（取笑时）兔子们正慌忙从洞里探头，／（探头是）想看看外面在闹什么。
column9: row 在这里读 /raʊ/，意思是“吵闹，争吵”，不是读 /rəʊ/ 的“一排”。what the row was about = 外面在闹什么。
column10: 老兔子一眨眼就被撞翻了。鼹鼠正不耐烦，也根本没把他放在眼里，沿着树篱一路小跑，边跑边取笑别的兔子；那些兔子正慌慌张张从洞里探出头来，想看看外面在闹什么。
column12: The Wind in the Willows 第 1 章 句 2

column2: But the Mole was bent on enjoying everything, and although just when he had got the basket packed and strapped up tightly he saw a plate staring up at him from the grass, and when the job had been done again the Rat pointed out a fork which anybody ought to have seen, and last of all, behold! the mustard pot, which he had been sitting on without knowing it—still, somehow, the thing got finished at last, without much loss of temper.
column3: strap 用带子扣紧；behold 瞧
column4: although 那一大段过去以后，主句的谓语是哪几个词？
column6: the Mole was … the thing got finished
column7: But the Mole was bent on enjoying everything, / and / although / just when he had got the basket packed / and strapped up tightly / he saw a plate / staring up at him from the grass, / and / when the job had been done again / the Rat pointed out a fork / which anybody ought to have seen, / and last of all, behold! / the mustard pot, / which he had been sitting on without knowing it— / still, somehow, the thing got finished at last, / without much loss of temper.
column8: 可鼹鼠一心要把什么都享受一遍，／而／虽然／他刚把篮子装好，／带子扣紧，／就看见一只盘子／在草地上抬眼瞪着他；／接着，／重新装好以后，／河鼠又指出一把叉子，／这（叉子）谁都早该看见；／最后，瞧！／芥末罐，／他（鼹鼠）一直坐在上面都不知道——／尽管这样，不知怎么，这事总算做完了，／也没怎么发脾气。
column9: although 引出的部分太长，到破折号还没出现主句。破折号后的 still 是“尽管如此”，接回 although；and 后面这一半的主句是 the thing got finished at last。
column10: 可鼹鼠一心要把什么都享受一遍。他刚把篮子装好、扣紧带子，就看见一只盘子躺在草地上瞪着他；好不容易重新装好，河鼠又指出一把叉子，那是谁都早该看见的；最后，瞧！还有芥末罐，鼹鼠一直坐在上面都不知道。尽管这样，不知怎么的，这件事最后总算做完了，也没怎么发脾气。
column12: The Wind in the Willows 第 1 章 句 6

column2: “Now, look here, Toad!” said the Rat sharply: “as soon as we get to the town, you’ll have to go straight to the police-station and see if they know anything about that motorcar and who it belongs to, and lodge a complaint against it.
column3: sharply 严厉地；motorcar 汽车；lodge a complaint 投诉
column4: who it belongs to 里，to 的宾语是哪个词？
column6: said the Rat … you’ll have to go … see … lodge
column7: “Now, look here, Toad!” / said the Rat sharply: / “as soon as we get to the town, / you’ll have to go straight to the police-station / and see if they know anything / about that motorcar / and who it belongs to, / and lodge a complaint against it.
column8: “喂，听着，蟾蜍！”／河鼠严厉地说：／“一到镇上，／你就得直接去警察局，／问问他们知不知道／那辆汽车的情况／和它（车）是谁的，／再告它（那辆车）一状。
column9: 读到 belongs to 容易以为 to 后面缺了宾语。who it belongs to 是套在 if 从句里的又一层，to 的宾语就是前面的 who：车是谁的。
column10: “喂，听着，蟾蜍！”河鼠严厉地说，“一到镇上，你就得直接去警察局，问问他们知不知道那辆汽车的情况、车主是谁，再告它一状。”
column12: The Wind in the Willows 第 2 章 卡句 3

column2: Rearing, plunging, backing steadily, in spite of all the Mole’s efforts at his head, and all the Mole’s lively language directed at his better feelings, he drove the cart backward towards the deep ditch at the side of the road.
column3: rear （马）后腿直立；plunge 往前猛冲；in spite of 不管，尽管；backward 向后
column4: 三个分词的动作，是后面哪个词发出的？
column7: Rearing, plunging, backing steadily, / in spite of all the Mole’s efforts at his head, / and all the Mole’s lively language / directed at his better feelings, / he drove the cart backward / towards the deep ditch at the side of the road.
column8: 又是直立，又是猛冲，一个劲儿往后退，／不管鼹鼠在马头那儿怎么使劲，／也不管鼹鼠说了多少激动的话／冲着他（马）的良心说的，／他（马）把车往后倒，／倒向路边的深沟。
column12: The Wind in the Willows 第 2 章 句 2

column2: Eventually, a slow train having landed them at a station not very far from Toad Hall, they escorted the spellbound, sleepwalking Toad to his door, put him inside it, and instructed his housekeeper to feed him, undress him, and put him to bed.
column3: escort 护送；spellbound 着了魔的；sleepwalk 梦游；instruct 吩咐
column4: having landed 的主语是哪几个词？
column7: Eventually, / a slow train having landed them / at a station not very far from Toad Hall, / they escorted the spellbound, sleepwalking Toad / to his door, / put him inside it, / and instructed his housekeeper / to feed him, undress him, and put him to bed.
column8: 最后，／一列慢车把他们送到／离蟾宫不太远的一个车站，／他们护送着了魔、梦游似的蟾蜍／到他家门口，／把他塞进门，／又吩咐他的管家／给他吃饭、脱衣服、送他上床。
column12: The Wind in the Willows 第 2 章 句 4

column2: It wavered an instant—then there was a heartrending crash—and the canary-coloured cart, their pride and their joy, lay on its side in the ditch, an irredeemable wreck.
column3: waver 摇晃；heartrending 令人心碎的；irredeemable 无法挽回的；wreck 残骸
column4: 拿掉插进来的部分，cart 后面接的是哪个词？
column6: It wavered … was a heartrending crash … the canary-coloured cart … lay
column7: It wavered an instant— / then there was a heartrending crash— / and the canary-coloured cart, / their pride and their joy, / lay on its side in the ditch, / an irredeemable wreck.
column8: 它（车）晃了一下——／接着是叫人心碎的一声巨响——／那辆金丝雀黄的篷车，／他们最得意的宝贝，／侧翻在沟里，／成了一堆没救的残骸。
column9: lay 是 lie（躺）的过去式，不是“放”。lay on its side 是车侧翻着躺在沟里。
column10: 车晃了一下，接着是叫人心碎的一声巨响，那辆金丝雀黄的篷车，他们最得意的宝贝，侧翻在沟里，成了一堆没救的残骸。
column12: The Wind in the Willows 第 2 章 句 3

column2: Naturally a voluble animal, and always mastered by his imagination, he painted the prospects of the trip and the joys of the open life and the roadside in such glowing colours that the Mole could hardly sit in his chair for excitement.
column3: voluble 话多的；master 支配；prospect 前景；glowing 鲜亮的
column4: Naturally a voluble animal 说的是哪个词？
column7: Naturally a voluble animal, / and always mastered by his imagination, / he painted the prospects of the trip / and the joys of the open life and the roadside / in such glowing colours / that the Mole could hardly sit in his chair / for excitement.
column8: （他）天生话多，／又总被想象牵着走，／他描绘这趟旅行的前景／和野外生活、路边风光的乐趣，／用的颜色那么鲜亮，／以至于鼹鼠在椅子上都快坐不住了——／（坐不住是因为）太兴奋了。
column9: Naturally a voluble animal 后面没有动词，补出来是 He was naturally a voluble animal。它和后面的 mastered 短语说的都是 he（蟾蜍）。
column10: 蟾蜍天生话多，又总让想象牵着走，他把这趟旅行的前景、野外生活和路边风光的乐趣说得天花乱坠，鼹鼠兴奋得在椅子上都快坐不住了。
column12: The Wind in the Willows 第 2 章 卡句 1

column2: After all, the best part of a holiday is perhaps not so much to be resting yourself, as to see all the other fellows busy working.
column4: 和 not so much 呼应的是哪个词？
column7: After all, / the best part of a holiday is perhaps / not so much to be resting yourself, / as to see all the other fellows busy working.
column8: 说到底，／假期最妙的地方，或许／与其说是自己歇着，／不如说是看着别的家伙都在忙活。
column9: not so much A as B 的重心在 B，意思是“与其说是 A，不如说是 B”，不是“没有 B 那么多”。这里说放假最妙的，主要不在自己歇着，而在看别人都在忙。
column10: 说到底，假期最妙的地方，或许与其说是自己歇着，倒不如说是看着别的家伙都在忙活。
column12: The Wind in the Willows 第 1 章 句 3

column2: As he sat on the grass and looked across the river, a dark hole in the bank opposite, just above the water’s edge, caught his eye, and dreamily he fell to considering what a nice, snug dwelling-place it would make for an animal with few wants and fond of a bijou riverside residence, above flood level and remote from noise and dust.
column3: dreamily 出神地；snug 舒适暖和的；riverside 河边的
column4: it would make 的 it 指什么？
column6: a dark hole … caught … he fell to
column7: As he sat on the grass / and looked across the river, / a dark hole in the bank opposite, / just above the water’s edge, / caught his eye, / and dreamily he fell to considering / what a nice, snug dwelling-place it would make / for an animal with few wants / and fond of a bijou riverside residence, / above flood level / and remote from noise and dust.
column8: 他坐在草地上，／望着河对岸，／对岸河堤上有个黑洞，／就在水边稍高一点的地方，／引起了他的注意，／他出神地琢磨起来：／它（那个洞）会是多舒服的住处啊——／给一只要求不多的动物住，／（这动物）又喜欢小巧的河畔住宅；／（这住宅）水淹不到，／又远离喧闹和尘土。
column9: it would make 的 make 不是“制造”，是“成为，适合当”：这个洞做个住处该多好。名词被 what 提到了前面，还原成陈述句是 it would make a nice, snug dwelling-place。
column10: 他坐在草地上望着河对岸，对岸水边稍高一点的地方有个黑洞，引起了他的注意。他出神地琢磨起来：有的动物要求不多，又喜欢小巧精致的河畔住宅——水淹不到，远离喧闹和尘土；这样的动物住在这儿该多舒服啊。
column12: The Wind in the Willows 第 1 章 句 4
